title: "Point Loading"
format: html
---

## Overview

Point data stores one $(x, y)$ coordinate per frame (for example: nose tip, tongue tip, whisker base).

Neuralyzer supports two point-loading paths:

| Path | Typical Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Data Import Widget | Manual import from a single CSV file | Exposes frame/x/y column mapping and delimiter selection |
| JSON configuration | Reproducible or batch workflows | Supports both simple CSV and DeepLabCut-style CSV |

::: {.callout-note}
## JSON Data Type Name
Use `"data_type": "points"` in JSON.
:::

## Data Import Widget (CSV)

Open **Modules -> Data Import**, choose **Point Data**, then load a CSV file.

Widget options:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `frame_column` | 0-based column index containing frame numbers |
| `x_column` | 0-based column index containing x coordinates |
| `y_column` | 0-based column index containing y coordinates |
| `column_delim` | Delimiter used to split columns (`Comma` or `Space` in the current widget) |

### Header behavior

The point CSV parser does not have a dedicated `has_header` toggle. Rows are accepted when `frame_column` is numeric; non-numeric frame rows are ignored.

## JSON: Simple CSV Point Format

Use `format: "csv"` for generic frame/x/y CSV files.

```json
{
	"filepath": "tracking/nose.csv",
	"data_type": "points",
	"name": "nose_tip",
	"format": "csv",
	"frame_column": 0,
	"x_column": 1,
	"y_column": 2,
	"column_delim": ",",
	"nan_handling": "Skip"
}
```

| Element | Required? | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `filepath` | Yes | string | - | Path to CSV file |
| `data_type` | Yes | string | - | Must be `"points"` |
| `name` | Yes | string | - | Output object name |
| `format` | Yes | string | - | `"csv"` |
| `frame_column` | No | integer | `0` | 0-based frame column |
| `x_column` | No | integer | `1` | 0-based x column |
| `y_column` | No | integer | `2` | 0-based y column |
| `column_delim` | No | string | space (`" "`) | Column delimiter (first character is used) |
| `nan_handling` | No | string | `"Skip"` | `"Skip"` drops rows with NaN coordinates; `"Include"` keeps them |
| `clock` | No | string | `"time"` | Assigns this data to an existing TimeFrame |

## JSON: DeepLabCut CSV Format

Use `format: "dlc_csv"` for DeepLabCut-style files with scorer/bodypart/coord header rows.

### Load one bodypart

```json
{
	"filepath": "tracking/dlc_output.csv",
	"data_type": "points",
	"name": "tongue_tip",
	"format": "dlc_csv",
	"bodypart": "tongue_tip",
	"frame_column": 0,
	"likelihood_threshold": 0.9
}
```

### Load all bodyparts from one file

```json
{
	"filepath": "tracking/dlc_output.csv",
	"data_type": "points",
	"name": "dlc",
	"format": "dlc_csv",
	"all_bodyparts": true,
	"frame_column": 0,
	"likelihood_threshold": 0.8
}
```

With `all_bodyparts: true`, one PointData object is created per bodypart.

| Element | Required? | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | Yes | string | - | `"dlc_csv"` |
| `bodypart` | No | string | first bodypart | Specific bodypart to load |
| `all_bodyparts` | No | boolean | `false` | Load all bodyparts as separate outputs |
| `frame_column` | No | integer | `0` | 0-based frame column |
| `likelihood_threshold` | No | number | `0.0` | Ignore samples below this likelihood |
